answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks by requiring each node to anchor its key to an acoustic delay ring. To register, a node must solve a memory-hard sequential cipher over a physical copper transmission line within a tight latency window. Influence is bounded to one vote per verified physical module. An attacker cannot bypass this with virtual clones, because running many identities forces the scarce capital expense of buying and operating separate physical copper delay hardware for every instance, rendering bulk identity forgery net-negative.
